The companies, along with their lawyers, discussed the plan earlier this year, where their competitor could poke and prod the latest available model, searching for unexpected dangers or vulnerabilities, the report said. The testing would only apply to commercially available models. They also agreed not to retain each other's data.
The report did not clarify if any type of agreement was eventually met.
CEO Elon Musk recommended that the leading U.S.-based LLM companies, along with several from China, should allow competitors to conduct testing and peer reviews.

“So, you know, instead of grading your own homework, you would at least have competitors grading your homework and raising the alarm if they see concerns,” Musk said during the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on September 14.
